transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM); Samir Iqbal (CTO), Rosa Chen (Platform Eng), Oliver Park (SRE), Hannah Lee (Security)

Auto-generated summary: short notes may be off — see action items.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we wanted to run through the egress branching topology you described and validate KV-cache behavior under the split egress. Lina is on to take notes.
[00:12] Samir (CTO): Yep, thanks. High level we have a private VPC in us-east-1 with multiple subnets for ingestion, inference, and analytics. We need inference traffic to go out via PrivateLink to Redwood private endpoints, but sometimes for failover we route through NATs to a backup egress. We're seeing p95 jitter when the egress path flips.
[00:30] Ethan (Redwood SE): Ok, can you say more about the failover? Is that a route-table change or some kind of live NAT translation?
[00:36] Rosa (Platform Eng): It's a route-table preference swap; primary subnets have a prefix that targets PrivateLink endpoints, backup routes send to a managed NAT GW. When we fail over we sometimes see half-open TCP and sticky connections.
[00:50] Oliver (SRE): Also we do hairpin for some internal testing where traffic from the same subnet goes out and returns — not ideal but helps with our debugging. The MTU sometimes drops to 1400 under the NAT path and that affects larger responses.
[01:05] Ethan: That MTU point is important — Redwood's runtime will break up tokens but underlying TCP fragmentation can increase latency. We typically recommend ensuring path MTU >= 1500 or enabling PMTU discovery; otherwise you'll see increased per-request tail latency for longer responses.
[01:20] Hannah (Security): From our side we need to confirm no egress leaves the customer's network unless encrypted and audited. How does Redwood log egress per-request and correlate to tokens?
[01:30] Maya: We have per-request tracing in the console and audit logs that show model, route, and egress path. We'll send the SOC2 packet. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and can push logs to your SIEM over secure forwarders.
[01:45] Samir: Cool. Back to KV-cache — we run long conversations for agents, and KV-cache eviction during route flips seems to cause rewarm and spikes. Is there a way to avoid eviction across PrivateLink vs NAT transitions?
[02:00] Ethan: Yes, a few notes. The KV cache is keyed by session and by the model variant and runtime instance identity. If a request is routed to a different worker pool (e.g., dedicated PrivateLink pool vs backup NAT pool that uses quantized variants) the cache cannot be reused. That causes cold starts. Two approaches: 1) sticky routing so the session stays on same pool, 2) prefix cache replication between compatible pools, or 3) fast rewarm heuristics that prefetch likely prefixes after a failover. We can demo option 2 in the lab but it has network cost.
[02:30] Rosa: Sticky routing is tricky for us because we want rapid failover at route table level. Prefetch might be better. What about batching impact? We rely on small batch sizes to keep latency low.
[02:45] Ethan: Smaller batches are lower latency but higher per-token cost. Under failover, batching won't save you if the request moves to new pool and requires KV rewarm. If you can tolerate a short rewarm hit, batching helps throughput overall. For the stress test we should simulate both small (<=4) and medium (8-16) batch mixes.
[03:05] Lina (CSM): Noted — we'll capture the representative traffic mix. Oliver, can you share a week of your p50/p95 traces?
[03:12] Oliver: I'll export and share tonight.
[03:16] Samir: Another weird incident — on one failover our DNS resolver returned different PrivateLink A records (round-robin) and traffic went to a different AZ with slightly different kernel tuning, and then the kv-cache warmed incorrectly. Any way to pin the resolver?
[03:30] Ethan: For PrivateLink we recommend using the VPC’s resolver with consistent TTLs and, when possible, route by endpoint ID rather than DNS. If you have split-horizon DNS we should ensure consistent answers across AZs. TTLs of 30s can be fine but if your route tables flip faster it won't help. Optionally, use an internal forwarding resolver in each subnet to ensure affinity.
[03:50] Rosa: If we forward to an internal resolver, does Redwood respect EDNS client subnet or is that lost? We rely on EDNS for geo-aware routing in some cases.
[04:00] Ethan: We don't currently use EDNS client subnet per-request; routing is done by VPC endpoint and instance metadata. EDNS could be preserved if your resolver retains it but not as a routing key inside the runtime.
[04:12] Hannah: On the security end, we need per-route mTLS and SNI validation. Do you support mTLS on PrivateLink?
[04:20] Maya: We support mTLS termination at the PrivateLink endpoint and require client certs for Dedicated/Private installs. We'll include the cert rotation cadence in the packet.
[04:30] Samir: Great. For the soak test: we need a 24h run across primary -> forced failover -> back to primary, and measure p95 latency, token drop, and cache miss rates. Can Redwood instrument cache hit ratio at per-session granularity?
[04:45] Ethan: Yes, we can instrument hit/miss per session and export metrics to Prometheus or Datadog. For the test we'll capture KV miss rate, rewarm time, p50/p95/p99, and packet/MTU retransmit counters.
[04:58] Rosa: Also include TCP half-open and connection churn metrics; we saw ephemeral sockets piling up during the last route swap.
[05:06] Ethan: We'll add those. Also want to flag quantization: if the backup pool uses an int8 quantized variant to save cost, the model outputs can differ slightly and you may see output flakiness. We'll include a regression diff on the test prompts to measure deltas.
[05:24] Samir: Hmm, we can't have output regressions in prod. Are there options to prevent fallback to quantized variants during failover?
[05:30] Ethan: Yes — policy-based routing can prevent fallback; you can pin sessions to non-quantized variants for high-sensitivity routes. Alternatively, we can set a fidelity threshold where fallback only occurs if latency SLA is violated for X seconds.
[05:45] Hannah: We'll likely require no quantized fallback for payments/compliance flows. For other low-risk flows we can accept quantized fallback if it's within a diff threshold. Please document the threshold configuration.
[06:00] Maya: We'll add config examples to the runbook.
[06:06] [06:06] Oliver: Quick question: when PKI rotations happen on our side, do connections drop and is there an automatic reconnect? We experienced a brief 3-5s blip during our last rotation.
[06:18] Ethan: Rotations can induce brief renegotiation; clients usually reconnect with little disruption but long-lived TCP sessions might drop. We recommend rolling cert rotations with session drain and a short grace period. We'll show a sample rolling plan in the lab docs.
[06:34] Samir: For the on-prem piece — we plan an air-gapped test where Redwood's private control plane is restricted and we run inference inside our VPC with a forward proxy for telemetry. Can Redwood support proxying logs out to our SIEM via an egress forwarder?
[06:50] Maya: Yes, we support push-based forwarders and a pull model with an agent. We'll need an allowlist of endpoints and ports; we'll provide the list.
[07:00] Lina: Recap of agreed items: 1) Redwood to run 24h KV-cache soak with representative traffic and forced route flips; 2) customer to provide route tables, NAT config, and DNS resolver behavior; 3) schedule on-prem connectivity lab; 4) Redwood to share SOC2/ISO summary and runbook with policy examples.
[07:20] Samir: Sounds good. On timings, can the soak start next week? We can keep a window for Wednesday night to Thursday.
[07:28] Ethan: We can start Wednesday 2026-04-29 02:00 UTC and will post live dashboards.
[07:35] Hannah: Please include a checklist for firewall ports, egress IPs, and MTU verification steps.
[07:42] Maya: Will do. We'll also attach a sample traffic generator config and a set of test prompts for the regression diff.
[07:50] Rosa: One more note: our infra team uses an internal tag set on ENIs to route traffic — will that interfere with PrivateLink per-enpoint selection?
[08:00] Ethan: Not directly, but if your routing logic relies on ENI tags to pick a NAT vs endpoint, ensure the tags persist during failover. We'll include a playbook to map tags to routing tables.
[08:10] Samir: Ok thanks everyone.
[08:14] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the runbook and the SOC2 packet. Lina will send calendar invites for the lab.

End transcript.
